meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_55_packages.json, all reference===55 edges from torahData.js, and the full source text torah_55.txt. For each bechina statement in the source text, verified whether the concept appears as a node in the dataset. Only concepts with explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ, נִקְרָא) were considered for addition. Concepts that are purely eitza (causal) or are verse-proof citations rather than conceptual equivalences were excluded.

Suggested as an alias/expansion of the 'גם' node in the existing dataset rather than a new independent node.

The Rebbe explicitly defines שור (the word used in Balaam's vision) as bechina of הִסְתַּכְּלוּת (gazing/contemplation). The context is that the פרה אדומה receives from the 'שור' (ox), which is the bechina of gazing upward ('אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי אֶל הֶהָרִים' = gazing toward the mountains = perceiving God's justice = the action that leads to prayer). This הסתכלות is the act of seeing God's righteousness that straightens the heart (ישרת לב = אמונה = prayer). The שור/הסתכלות bechina is NOT currently in the dataset for Torah #55 and belongs in the prayer package as the cognitive act that enables emunah and prayer.

In the teaching's framework, ארז belongs with the prayer domain because the three items of the Parah Adumah (ארז, אזוב, שני תולעת) each correspond to a type of 'false voice' that prayer must rectify. Since אזוב is already in the dataset (edge 2629, reference=55), ארז should be added alongside it. Polarity is evil because it represents the fool's false speech that contaminates prayer.

However, this is a Zohar-cited teaching integrated into the proof-text of the teaching rather than a new bechina introduced by the Rebbe himself. This is filed as part of the new package proposal (torah_55_new_packages.json) rather than an addition to Package 2, because it forms part of the independent Parah Adumah components cluster.

Section ט (line 63): 'וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת כְּלָלִיּוּת מַלְאָךְ סנד"ל בַּמַּלְאָךְ מט"ט שַׂר הַפָּנִים, כְּלָלִיּוּת עֲשִׂיָּה בִּיצִירָה'. This introduces the Sandalfon/Metatron angelological framework as a bechina of the relationship between עשיה (action) and יצירה (formation). While structurally interesting, this appears at the very end of the teaching as a kabbalistic framework reference rather than as a primary bechina node the Rebbe is establishing. The 'זֶהוּ בְּחִינַת' formula is used but the referent is a kabbalah-technical cross-reference. This would require adding 4+ nodes from a different conceptual domain (angels, sefirot-worlds) that are not developed in the body of this Torah. Excluded from additions; flagged as potential future enrichment.

Section ח (line 46): 'זֶה בְּחִינַת תִּקּוּן הַתְּפִלָּה, בְּחִינַת דְּרִיכַת הַקֶּשֶׁת, בְּחִינַת הַתְּפִלָּה'. The bow (קשת) and its three colors = the Avot's light are identified with tikkun ha-tefillah. However, this appears in an eitza context ('על ידי זה' = through prayer, you inherit the Land). The קשת here is used as a metaphor for the three-colored bow = three Avot = three daily prayers, serving as the mechanism by which tefillah illuminates. While 'בְּחִינַת הַתְּפִלָּה' is used, it is applied to the entire clause of 'קַוֵּה אֶל ה' וּשְׁמֹר דַּרְכּוֹ' (tikkun ha-tefillah), not specifically a new node. This could be a dataset addition (קשת = תפלה) but it operates primarily in the eitza chain rather than as an independent bechina package member. Excluded pending further review.
